findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the supplied address with an exact `where(email: email)` match, and neither BlockedEmail nor EmailValidator normalizes case or surrounding whitespace before lookup/storage. A blocked address such as bad@spam.example can therefore be resubmitted as Bad@Spam.Example and will not match, bypassing the block even though mail delivery treats the domain case-insensitively. Normalize (at minimum downcase/strip) both when creating BlockedEmail records and when checking them.

findings.title: match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: should_block? does `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save`. Two concurrent registration attempts matching the same blocked email can both read the same match_count and both write count+1, losing an increment, and the full save also runs validations/callbacks on a hot validation path. Use an atomic increment (e.g. update_counters/increment_counter with last_match_at updated via update_all) instead.

findings.title: Validation has a write side effect and double-counts a single signup attempt
findings.body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and writes last_match_at. Validations run repeatedly for one logical attempt: UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save (which validates again), so one blocked signup is counted at least twice, and any other code that merely checks user.valid? (tests, console, unrelated flows) also falsely records a match. The statistics update should happen once per actual blocked attempt, not inside a reusable EachValidator.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array is shared mutable prototype state
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` declares one array on the controller prototype, so pushObject in createAccount mutates state shared by every instance of CreateAccountController rather than per-instance state. Rejected addresses can leak between controller instances (notably tests and any non-singleton use) and are never reset. Initialize the array per instance (e.g. in init) and clear it when the modal/account flow is reset.
